messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: unusual traffic pattern detected from multiple proxy ASNs hitting /v1/generate. 99th p90 latency increased to 1.8s, error rate 5% (429s), tokens/sec spiked to 4.2M. Auto-throttle triggered. See logs: 
ops-bot: ```
src: 52.34.12.1, ASN 16509, requests: 12k/min, path: /v1/generate, user_agent: python-requests/2.28
error: 429 rate_limited, backend_latency: 1800ms
```
sanjay: paging oncall. I'm looking. Suspect proxy farm + credential stuffing on older endpoints.
sanjay: quick status: can we confirm which customers are affected? 
support-alex: support ticketing shows 4 high-volume customers seeing 429s since 15:02 UTC. One is a public crawl job we flagged earlier but not blocked.
leo: I can push a temporary global rate limit on /v1/generate to 60 reqs/min per IP and 5 reqs/min per user-token. That should shed load. Anyone object?
nina: do the per-IP limit first; per-token may impact legitimate bots. Also suggest enabling WAF rule to block ASN ranges we see in hits.
sanjay: agree. leo, push the IP rate limit + add a soft quota bump for paid customers to avoid impacting them.
leo: applying rate limit now via gateway: 
leo: ```
mgmtctl apply-rate-limit --path /v1/generate --per-ip 60/m --per-token 300/m --priority temporary_abuse
```
leo: done. gateway reports config version 5879, rolling out.
ops-bot: config rollout started by leo (cfg-5879).
leo: also adding a WAF CIDR block for the top offending ASN to test: 
leo: ```
wafctl add-block --name temp-asn-16509 --cidr 52.32.0.0/14 --reason "abuse: proxy farm" --duration 2h
```
leo: waf rule applied, action=block, id=waf-931.
nina: nice. Sanjay, can you start collecting customer-impact list for comms? Which customers saw degraded throughput vs total 429s?
sanjay: copying stats: overall 14% of requests were throttled after the rate-limit; for paid customers that dropped to 1.2% thanks to quota bump. A few free-tier API keys hit hard.
sanjay: mitigation observed immediate drop in tokens/sec to 1.1M, latencies back to 250-400ms p95. Error rate down to 0.7%.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Postmortem ticket created: INC-2026-0421, severity P1, lead=sanjay.
support-alex: created support thread and flagged impacted accounts; drafting outbound note for customers with sustained failures.
sanjay: two tasks: (1) iterate WAF blocks to cover proxy ASN ranges (collect list), (2) durable long-term quota config for bursty free-tier abuse. Assigning (1) to leo, (2) to nina.
leo: ack. I'll query flow logs and ASN mapping, will escalate rare-IP false positives if needed.
nina: I'll draft quota change RFC to be reviewed by product — likely add a sliding window token bucket for free-tier with strict burst cap.
sanjay: starting on-call handoff in 10m. Quick summary for next oncall: 
- what happened: proxy-fanout scraper/credential-stuffing increased request volume to /v1/generate; gateway auto-throttled but still impacted free-tier customers.
- mitigation applied: temporary per-IP rate limits (60/m), soft per-token quotas for paid customers, WAF block for ASN 16509 (waf-931).
- current status: traffic normalized; monitoring for evasion and new ASNs.
- open actions: expand ASN blocklist (leo), permanent quota change RFC (nina), customer comms (support-alex), postmortem writeup (sanjay).
sanjay: handing over to nina for the night. Full logs and runbook link: https://redwood.internal/ops/runbooks/abuse-mitigation
nina: taking over. I'll keep waf rule and rate limit locked for now. If anything looks like false-positive, ping me on this thread.
leo: one more note, we observed requests reusing older model checkpoints with high token counts; consider temporary model-size cap for anonymous keys.
sanjay: good point. Add to postmortem.
incident-bot: :pager: Oncall handoff recorded: from sanjay to nina at 2026-04-21T15:18:10Z.
support-alex: sending initial customer advisory now: "We experienced elevated 429s due to abusive traffic. Mitigations applied; if you still see errors please reply to this ticket."
nina: thanks team. I'll monitor alerts and escalate to infra if blocks start affecting EU region.
leo: will follow up with ASN list and log dump in this thread in 20m.
sanjay: closing my pager. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
